title: Perez signs Cadillac contract extension until at least 2029
excerpt:
Sergio Perez has extended his contract with the Cadillac Formula 1 Team, ensuring the Mexican driver will remain with the American outfit until at least 2029.

Cadillac announced on Wednesday ahead of the Mexico City Grand Prix that they had retained the services of Perez, who joined the project ahead of the team’s F1 debut in 2026.

“Joining Cadillac Formula 1 Team from day one was a project I truly believed in, and extending my commitment feels like a natural continuation of this chapter,” said Perez.

“Building a Formula 1 team from the ground up takes time, relentless work and patience, but the progress we are making together is incredibly rewarding. There is still a lot of work ahead of us and I am fully committed for the next three years.

“I want to thank Dan (Towriss), Mark (Reuss), and everyone at TWG Motorsports and General Motors for the opportunity to build on what we have started together. To every member of this special team, at the track, in the US, the UK, and our fans, thank you for your support and trust. I won’t let you down. Let’s keep pushing!”

Perez has taken six Grand Prix wins during a career that has included spells at Sauber, McLaren, Force India, Racing Point and Red Bull, and will make his 300th F1 start in front of his home fans this weekend in Mexico City.

Although Perez and Cadillac have yet to score a point this season, the team have steadily improved over the course of the 2026 campaign as they look to move further up the grid.

“On the eve of a special weekend in Mexico City, we’re thrilled to announce that Checo will remain an integral part of Cadillac Formula 1 Team for years to come,” said Dan Towriss, CEO, Cadillac Formula 1 Team.

“Building a competitive team in F1 is a long-term journey, and securing Checo’s talent and leadership gives us the continuity and commitment we need to build on the strong foundation established in our first year.

"Together, we are focused on the next phase of our journey, pushing the team forward and making progress up the grid.”

title: Formula 1 publishes first sport-wide Social Impact Report
excerpt:
Formula 1 has today published its first sport-wide Social Impact Report, revealing that more than 500,000 young people across 71 countries accessed and benefitted from Formula 1 programmes designed to educate, inspire and open pathways into the sport in 2025.

Alongside the report, Formula 1 has renewed its flagship Engineering Scholarship for a further three academic years, committing more than £2.4 million in funding. Founded in 2021, the scholarship programme addresses some of the key barriers to higher education for these students including the financial burden and accessing opportunities and has supported 48 students to date.

The programme covers full tuition fees and living costs for students from underrepresented backgrounds, giving them unrivalled access to Formula 1 through placements with F1 teams, exposure to the world-class technology behind the fastest cars in motorsport, exclusive visits to the Formula 1 Media and Technology Centre, and behind-the-scenes experiences at Grand Prix weekends.

Ten new scholars will join each year from 2026/27 to 2028/29, studying at the University of Strathclyde, Imperial College London, the University of Cambridge, the University of Oxford, and MUNER in Italy.

The report brings together, for the first time, the collective contribution of Formula 1, the FIA, all 10 teams and 24 race promoters during the 2025 season. It marks an important milestone in the sport’s efforts and on the recommendations of The Hamilton Commission, launched by Sir Lewis Hamilton and the Royal Academy of Engineering in 2021, and follows the publication of the sport’s first Diversity and Inclusion Charter, signed by Formula 1, the FIA and all 10 teams in 2024 (the Cadillac F1 Team signed the charter from the 2026 season, when they entered the sport).

Together, the report and scholarship renewal demonstrate how the sport is working to create opportunities for underrepresented groups, inspire future talent and make motorsport more accessible to all.

With 24 races across 21 countries, a fanbase of more than 830 million people and a cumulative annual television audience of 1.7 billion, Formula 1 is uniquely positioned to inspire future generations and broaden access to opportunities within motorsport. Initiatives such as the British Council’s Learning Sectors education programme, which has worked with more than 150,000 students across four countries in STEM learning, promoter-led community activities delivered at all 24 Grands Prix, and charitable fundraising efforts all help to achieve this ambition.

2025 highlights include:

500,000+ young people given access to the sport through education, STEM and inspiration programmes globally

100% of Diversity and Inclusion Charter signatories delivering social impact programmes

1,000+ skills and talent development opportunities spotlighting motorsport and related industries

10 students awarded the Formula 1 Engineering Scholarship in 2025, taking the total supported since the scheme launched in 2021 to 48

£2.4 million committed to renew the Formula 1 Engineering Scholarship until at least 2028/29, supporting 10 new students each year with tuition fees and living expenses

29,000+ schools compete annually in the STEM Racing global education initiative

700+ schools across the UK, South Africa, India and Brazil participated in the British Council’s Learning Sectors education programme

€100,000 donations given to four organisations awarded the F1 Allwyn Global Community Award

2,500+ young people participating in activities delivered at Formula 1 events

50+ wishes granted through Formula 1's partnership with Make-A-Wish

140 young people attended F1 Academy workshops

Formula 1 will continue to expand programmes highlighted in the report, including Learning Sectors and the F1 Allwyn Global Community Award, reaching more children and communities around the world. The sport will strengthen its approach to governance, measurement and reporting to better understand results, share progress and maximise the long-term value of its social impact work.

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1, said: “Formula 1 has an extraordinary power to inspire, and we want everyone to believe there is a place for them in our sport. We are turning our commitments into action, working across motorsport to break down barriers and widen access for future generations.

“We are proud of the progress made and grateful for the collective efforts of Lewis Hamilton, the Hamilton Commission, the FIA, our teams, race promoters, partners and the many organisations helping to create lasting change. By renewing the Formula 1 Engineering Scholarship for a further three academic years and investing in young people and communities, we will open more doors, nurture talent and inspire the next generation to believe that a future in Formula 1 is within their reach.”

Ellen Jones, Head of ESG at Formula 1, said: “As Formula 1 continues to grow around the world, so does our ambition to build positive change beyond the track. This report provides, for the first time, a collective view of the impact programmes being delivered across the sport and the difference they are making in communities globally.

“From STEM education and skills development to charitable partnerships and initiatives that improve access to motorsport, these programmes are helping young people build confidence, develop future-ready skills and explore new career opportunities.

“The renewal of the Formula 1 Engineering Scholarship builds on the progress captured in this report, offering sustained support that can remove financial barriers and help more students from underrepresented backgrounds take their first steps towards engineering careers. We look forward to continuing to work across the sport to strengthen and expand this work in the years ahead.”

title: Ricciardo opens up on the ‘humiliation’ he felt amid F1 exit
excerpt:
Former Red Bull and McLaren driver Daniel Ricciardo has opened up on the impact of his sudden retirement from F1 in 2024, explaining that while he initially had feelings of “failure and humiliation”, he’s now proud of his career.

The Aussie was a key figure on the grid between 2011, when he made his mid-season debut with HRT, and 2024, achieving eight Grand Prix victories and a further 24 podiums in that time.

Ricciardo was renowned for his aggressive, late-braking driving style and infectious personality, but departed the sport immediately after the 2024 Singapore Grand Prix following a frustrating season with Racing Bulls.

“You start racing at such a young age and over the years you build a ruthlessness, but that also is inward as well,” Ricciardo explained on the latest episode of official podcast F1 Beyond The Grid. “You know, you can be very harsh on yourself and expect a lot from yourself.

“I think that my view of it was [that I was] failing, not performing to the level I needed to at the time or not being able to finish out the season or whatever. It's then a sense of humiliation, like I failed and I didn't do what I once could. Trying to deal with those next few months, I understood it as I was just hiding from the humiliation.

“People saw me out in public. I was having a good time and having a drink or whatever, and I was just really hiding from what I really felt deep inside, which was a lot of pain and sadness. You know, I was once this kid that was hoping at least to fight for a world title and obviously winning races or whatever, but now it's like, oh, it's gone.”

Despite the disappointment around his retirement, Ricciardo admitted that he now appreciates Racing Bulls’ decision to replace him with Liam Lawson as it gave him the chance to find a life outside of F1.

He said: “Everyone's path is going to be different. I think actually the fear I had, in hindsight and learning how content I am not having that anymore, is that what if they kept just extending contracts for me? Would I keep doing it? Was I ever going to turn the tap off?

“I know I wanted to at times. I can tell you right now in Monaco 2022 after the race, I'm sitting in my apartment talking to my team and I was like, ‘I don't want to do this anymore. I'm done’.

Ranking Daniel Ricciardo's 8 Grand Prix wins

“And I've had these conversations more than once over the years – Silverstone 2015 was another time. Sure, you have lows and whatever, but there's moments where I've wanted to just get away from it. But the reality is, would I have?

“I also think you have people around you that tell you a great tale, you can still do it, and you end up believing a lot of these voices. I know they don't mean harm but you don't really get a chance to have your own thoughts much.

“I think that would have probably just continued, and maybe I'd still be racing and that's also a scary thought. I still don't like how it ended, but there's also a part of me which is grateful that they pulled the trigger because I wouldn't want to be doing it now.”

Although Ricciardo isn’t certain whether he’ll return to racing in another series quite yet, he admitted that with the benefit of hindsight, he’s reached a stage where he can reflect on his F1 career – which included spectacular wins in Monaco and Monza – with a sense of pride.

“In the aftermath of everything, I use the word failure and humiliation in these things, and I appreciate a lot of the stuff I've said probably feels very negative or heavy,” he summarised. “But now that I'm out of that, I think being able to understand more [about] life and a lot of things around that, I look back now with much more of a smile than I did a couple years ago.

“I am definitely proud. I think sometimes you also never really want to reflect that much, especially when you're racing, because you nearly spook yourself. If I'm like, ‘Oh wow, I did that’, you’re just like, no, can't think about that. I’ve just got to stay on it because it was all just weird for me.

“Maybe every F1 driver feels this, I don't know, but there's so few of us. It's not imposter syndrome because I believe I was definitely good enough to be there and all that, but it's like, how did this happen? You know, how am I one of the 20?

“I've won races. It can be overwhelming to reflect. But now that I'm in, let's say a good, even-keeled place, I'm extremely proud, shocked in many ways that it all happened.”

title: What time is the 2026 Mexico City GP and how can I watch it?
excerpt:
The 2026 Formula 1 season heads to Mexico City next for the 19th race weekend of the campaign, with the drivers barely having time to catch their breath after racing in Austin last Sunday.

Kimi Antonelli took the victory at the Circuit of The Americas in dominant fashion for Mercedes, leaving him on the cusp of a historic Drivers’ title, which he looks likely to wrap up at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.

George Russell and Lewis Hamilton are the only two who can stop the Italian, but both will need to win this weekend to stand any chance of keeping their title hopes alive.

Head to the RACE HUB or scroll down for more on how and when you can watch the action, along with the global start times for each session.

What time is the Mexico City Grand Prix?

The weekend will kick off with Free Practice 1 at 1230 local time on Friday, 30 October, followed by Free Practice 2 later that day at 1600.

A final hour of practice will begin at 1130 on Saturday, 31 October, before Qualifying gets underway at 1500. The Grand Prix itself will take place at 1400 on Sunday, 01 November.

Check out the image below to find all the global start times for Sunday’s race.

How can I watch the Mexico City Grand Prix?

You can enjoy coverage from every session live on F1 TV Pro (available in selected countries), which brings fans closer to the action via exclusive features like onboard cameras on all 22 of the drivers’ cars, and access to both Pre-Race and Post-Race Shows.

F1 TV Pro can be streamed easily via Apple TV, Chromecast Generation 2 and above, Android TV, Google TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Roku. F1 TV Pro is free of ad breaks and available with commentary in six languages.

Fans can also watch via F1 TV Premium, a premier service that invites fans to step into the heart of the action with the ability to watch races in 4K Ultra HD/HDR on up to six different devices, as well as a personalised Multiview feature available on select devices with 26 different feeds to choose from.

Viewers can watch every F1 Grand Prix, F1 Sprint, Qualifying and practice session live in 4K Ultra HD/HDR at home, with F2, F3, F1 ACADEMY and Porsche Supercup sessions also available to watch live on the platform.

Alternatively, live timing will be available on F1.com and the F1 app across every session during the Grand Prix weekend.

Where is the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix taking place?

The Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez will host the 19th Grand Prix of the season, a track renowned for its atmosphere with the event often happening alongside the national holiday of Dia de Muertos.

This iconic circuit returned to the calendar in 2015, and has become a fan favourite ever since.

From the long start/finish straight to the raucous stadium section, the circuit offers plenty of character and makes for a breathless experience given its high altitude, which requires some lateral thinking from the teams in terms of car and brake cooling.

The weekend looks set to be warm and sunny, with temperatures just a few degrees cooler than the drivers enjoyed in Austin.

But there could be some showers around for Friday practice, so the teams will keep an eye on the skies to see if those materialise. The weather is generally good in Mexico, so whether that threat recedes and all three days of track action are run in sunny conditions remains to be seen.

title: Who impressed our Power Rankings judges in Austin?
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli took another step towards the 2026 world title with a superb display at the Circuit of The Americas in Austin. But who else impressed our Power Rankings judges?

Check out the latest scores and overall leaderboard below...

How it works

Our five-judge panel assess each driver after every Grand Prix and score them out of 10 according to their performance across the weekend – taking machinery out of the equation

Our experts’ scores are then averaged out to produce a race score – with those scores then tallied up across the season on our overall Power Rankings Leaderboard (at the bottom of the page)

Antonelli delivered a Qualifying and Grand Prix performance worthy of a World Champion last weekend – charging to both pole position and the race win. Despite Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc’s best efforts, the young Italian was simply unstoppable, and he now has another finger on the 2026 Drivers’ Championship trophy.

As the wait goes on to find out if he will keep his seat for 2027, Liam Lawson made another statement to Red Bull and Racing Bulls chiefs in the United States with his latest Q3 showing and points result. He has now scored in 13 of the 17 Grands Prix he has finished this year, and only appears to be growing in confidence and maturity.

After topping Friday practice and leading the way in Q2, Leclerc was left searching for answers when he ended up P4 in Qualifying – track conditions appearing to move away from Ferrari at the critical moment. He made up for it at the race start by passing Isack Hadjar off the line and then Verstappen with a bold move through the esses, and ended the day as Antonelli’s nearest challenger.

Verstappen arrived in Austin off the back of victories in Malaysia and Singapore, and he seemed to be in the mix for another win when he qualified on the front row of the grid. Race day was more of a challenge for the Dutchman, though, with a compromised start, a tyre strategy that he openly questioned and various technical issues. Nonetheless, he battled on and came away with a podium.

Pierre Gasly continued to wring the neck of Alpine’s package at the Circuit of The Americas, with the Frenchman getting close to Q3 in Qualifying and taking the fight to the cars ahead on race day. A well-earned point, which denied Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg and the other Racing Bulls of Arvid Lindblad, was his reward this time out – even after picking up damage in a scrap with Haas’ Ollie Bearman (for which the latter earned a penalty).

Lewis Hamilton started Sunday’s race from fifth position, just behind team mate Leclerc, but lost ground to the front-runners in the opening stint after lining up with used tyres – the only driver in the field to do so. His “biggest issue” as the encounter progressed, however, was the SF-26’s balance feeling “off”. A more competitive final stint saw him close back in on the podium places, but he ultimately had to settle for fourth.

Hadjar was one of the stars of Qualifying at the Circuit of The Americas with his P3 effort – sorting out an “undriveable” Red Bull in Friday practice to finish just a few hundredths down on team mate Verstappen. Unfortunately for the Frenchman, after that strong recovery, “everything went wrong” in the race. Like Verstappen, he was left frustrated by a sluggish start, before getting stuck in an incorrect engine map following a pit stop, which heavily compromised his pace en route to a P6 result.

You could forgive Hulkenberg for having nightmares about the number 11 this season – given how many times he has finished there in Qualifying sessions and Grands Prix. After coming close to Q3, and putting up a spirited midfield fight on race day, 11th proved to be the maximum for the German. It was another very solid performance, though, as Audi continue to lay foundations for the future.

Lando Norris was a man of few words after a track limits violation left him eighth on the grid for the United States Grand Prix – the McLaren man stating that he did a “c*** job”. He managed to make some progress during the race to turn that into a more respectable fifth position, comfortably ahead of team mate Oscar Piastri, as both drivers stuck it out on ageing tyres and adopted a one-stop strategy.

Despite some pre-race technical concerns over his car, Fernando Alonso enjoyed a strong start to Sunday’s Grand Prix – rising from 15th to 12th and knocking on the door of the points-paying positions. However, in his own words, the damage sustained from contact with Williams’ Alex Albon “compromised everything for us”. Alonso eventually had to pit for a new front wing, which dropped him down the order, but there were at least some performance positives to take away from the weekend.

Lindblad headed into the Austin weekend knowing he would be taking an engine-related grid penalty. That turned a strong P9 on the grid (after team mate Lawson opted against running in Q3) into P14, and left him with an uphill struggle to score points. After early contact with Carlos Sainz’s Williams, he gave it his all to recover the lost ground and make it back into the top-10 positions, but 12th was the limit in a fiercely competitive midfield fight.

Missing out

Just missing out on this week’s Power Rankings leaderboard are Haas’ Esteban Ocon (14th, after clearing team mate Bearman early on) and Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto (13th, from a back-of-the-grid engine penalty).

title: Breaking: Cadillac confirm F1 driver for 2027 on multi-year deal
excerpt:
Cadillac has confirmed Sergio Perez's position within the team for the 2027 campaign, annoucing a multi-year deal with the Mexican driver.

Perez joined Cadillac for the 2027 campaign as the American squad embarked on its first campaign on the F1 grid.

Perez formed one half of a vastly experienced line-up at the sport's newest team, with Valtteri Bottas fulfilling duties in the second car.

As Perez prepares to make his 300th race start on home soil this weekend at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, Cadillac has reaffirmed Perez's position within the team.

Joining Cadillac from day one was a project I truly believed in, and extending my commitment feels like a natural continuation of this chapter,” Perez said.

“Building a Formula 1 team from the ground up takes time, relentless work and patience, but the progress we are making together is incredibly rewarding.

“There is still a lot of work ahead of us and I am fully committed for the next three years.

“I want to thank Dan [Towriss], Mark [Reuss] and everyone at TWG Motorsports and General Motors for the opportunity to build on what we have started together.

“To every member of this special team, at the track, in the US, the UK, and our fans, thank you for your support and trust. I won’t let you down. Let’s keep pushing!”

Perez and Cadillac are still awaiting their first points of the year, with the 36-year-old's best result this far in 2026 being a 14th-place finish.

Team CEO Dan Towriss said of Perez's extension: “On the eve of a special weekend in Mexico City, we’re thrilled to announce that Checo will remain an integral part of the Cadillac team for years to come.

“Building a competitive team in F1 is a long-term journey, and securing Checo’s talent and leadership gives us the continuity and commitment we need to build on the strong foundation established in our first year.

“Together, we are focused on the next phase of our journey, pushing the team forward and making progress up the grid.”

title: F1 champions vital cause with multi-million-pound investment and important report
excerpt:
Formula 1 has announced a £2.4 million investment in its Engineering Scholarship programme alongside the publication of its first sport-wide Social Impact Report, highlighting efforts to make motorsport more accessible to underrepresented groups.

The report reveals that more than 500,000 young people across 71 countries benefited from education, STEM and community outreach initiatives delivered throughout 2025.

The findings bring together the contributions of F1, the FIA, all 10 teams and 24 race promoters, demonstrating the sport's commitment to improving diversity and accessibility.

The initiatives also build on recommendations made by the Hamilton Commission, established by seven-time F1 drivers' champion Lewis Hamilton and the Royal Academy of Engineering in 2021.

F1 has committed more than £2.4 million to extend its Engineering Scholarship programme for another three academic years, through to 2028/29.

Launched in 2021, the initiative has supported 48 students from underrepresented backgrounds, covering tuition fees and living expenses while providing placements with F1 teams. A further 10 students will join annually over the next three years.

F1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali said: "Formula 1 has an extraordinary power to inspire, and we want everyone to believe there is a place for them in our sport.

"We are turning our commitments into action, working across motorsport to break down barriers and widen access for future generations."

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem welcomed the findings and continued investment.

"Motorsport has the power to transform lives, and we have a responsibility to ensure its benefits reach beyond the racetrack," he said.

"Together, we are breaking down barriers, developing future talent and creating new pathways into our sport."

[Article continues below]

The report also highlights more than 1,000 skills and talent development opportunities, while over 29,000 schools participate annually in the STEM Racing initiative.

More than 150,000 students across four countries have also benefited from the British Council's Learning Sectors education programme.

F1's head of ESG, Ellen Jones, described the scholarship renewal as "offering sustained support that can remove financial barriers and help more students from underrepresented backgrounds take their first steps towards engineering careers".

UK skills minister Jacqui Smith MP also praised the initiative.

"Engineering is one of the industries most critical to our economic future, and we need more young people, from all backgrounds, to see it as a career for them," she said.

F1 intends to expand its existing programmes while strengthening how its impact is measured and reported.

title: Fernando Alonso reveals astonishing scale of US GP car damage
excerpt:
Fernando Alonso entered the United States Grand Prix hoping to score points, but his race unravelled after an opening lap collision.

Fernando Alonso believes a rare point-scoring opportunity was on the cards for Aston Martin at the United States Grand Prix.

The Spaniard lined up in 12th place after a positive qualifying outing on Saturday, but his race quickly unravelled when he was involved in a collision with Alex Albon on the opening lap.

It led Alonso to criticise the quality of the drivers towards the back of the F1 pack.

The two-time champion explained the extent of his car damage after the race, suggesting he was losing at least half a second per lap.

"I'd been hit by Alex in Turn 11, I think," Alonso told media including RacingNews365.

"That was the biggest damage. I think we lost like half a second or more.

"The car is destroyed. I saw it in parc fermé; half of the floor is not there. I don't know how we kept on going and how we were semi-competitive.

"So I imagine if the car was in one piece, probably today the points were a strong possibility, because we were running P12 with half a car."

[Article continues below]

'P9, P10 was possible' - Alonso

Aston Martin has scored seven points this year, with its last top 10 finish coming earlier this month at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Having had hopes of adding to the team's tally at the Circuit of the Americas, Alonso was forced to rue what might have been.

"One side of the floor was there and one side not," he said. "That was quite impressive what the car was able to do.

"It remains a little bit a curiosity of, with a full car performance, what we could have done.

"Probably P9, P10, points on merit was possible."

title: 2026 F1 Mexican Grand Prix - Mexico City weather forecast
excerpt:
2026 F1 Mexican Grand Prix - Mexico City weather forecast

Teams arriving at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez this week can expect largely settled conditions across the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend, with only a brief rain threat on Friday afternoon.

Friday's opening practice session is forecast to bring temperatures of 21°C to 23°C, sunny intervals and a gentle northerly breeze, giving drivers a relatively comfortable first look at the high-altitude circuit.

Conditions are expected to warm slightly for FP2, with the mercury rising to 26°C, though a higher chance of rainfall is forecast compared with the rest of the weekend. Showers are considered unlikely to actually materialise, however, with the session expected to stay dry.

Saturday's build-up to qualifying looks cooler and calmer. FP3 is expected to see temperatures drop back to 20°C to 21°C, under sunny skies with a gentle northerly wind similar to Friday morning.

Qualifying itself is forecast to be a touch warmer at 25°C, still under sunny conditions, though with stronger wind than in final practice, albeit still within gentle limits.

Sunday's race is expected to take place in 24°C sunny conditions, with no rain in the forecast.

That should offer some reassurance to teams managing the unique demands of the 2,200-metre-plus altitude venue, where thinner air already reduces downforce and increases strain on cooling systems and turbochargers regardless of ambient temperature.

With Pirelli having nominated its softest three compounds, the C3, C4 and C5, for the round, stable and dry conditions throughout the weekend should allow teams to focus purely on managing degradation and graining rather than variable grip from changing weather.

title: Kimi Antonelli reveals if he will choose driver number '1' as F1 champion
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli has revealed he will stick with the number '12' for 2027, even if he enters the year as the reigning champion.

Drivers who win the title are eligible to use number '1', as it is solely reserved for the driver who most recently topped the standings.

This year, it is being run by McLaren's Lando Norris, who clinched his maiden title at last year's Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

The Briton took over the rights to the number from Max Verstappen, who had it attached to his Red Bull from 2022 to 2025 during his years as the reigning champion.

Antonelli enters this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix with a high chance of securing the title, needing only ninth on the road on Sunday to become the sport's youngest ever champion.

He will then be able to choose his number for 2027, but the Italian has no interest in changing.

"First, I have to get the job done in Mexico. But I think that once that's done, I'll still be racing with number 12," Antonelli told Blick.

The only driver who previously passed up on the option to run number 1 as the champion since the introduction of the rule in 2014 was Lewis Hamilton, who retained '44' during his successful stint with Mercedes.

Antonelli has several reasons why the number 12 is so special to him. First, it's a tribute to his great idol: Ayrton Senna.

The Brazilian raced with that number between 1985 and 1988 and also won his first world title with it at McLaren.

In addition, 12 was also Antonelli's starting number when he made his debut in Formula 4, his first experience in a formula car. Furthermore, he was 12 years old when he was accepted into Mercedes' junior program.

title: Red Bull give first verdict on new Max Verstappen right-hand man
excerpt:
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has praised Tom Hart for his debut as Max Verstappen's race engineer in a "complicated" United States Grand Prix.

In the past, Simon Rennie has deputised for Gianpiero Lambiase in Verstappen's ear, but it was Hart who took over radio duties from 'GP', as he is affectionately known, at the Circuit of the Americas, as he gears up to assume the role full-time.

Lambiase is leaving the Milton Keynes-based team for McLaren imminently to become chief racing officer under Andrea Stella, so Red Bull has devised a plan to bed his replacement in.

Hart has worked at Red Bull since 2012 and has been closely involved with Verstappen's car since 2020 as a performance engineer.

To smooth the handover, the pair will split the remaining races between them. Hart will also be on the radio in São Paulo and Las Vegas, while Lambiase returns for Mexico City, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Verstappen finished third in Austin, behind pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc, but Mekies was pleased with how Hart's debut went in an otherwise disappointing afternoon for the four-time F1 drivers' champion.

"Look, I think he did an excellent job," Mekies said of Hart, when speaking to media, including RacingNews365, after the race.

"You see me smiling, because I certainly remember what it is to be on your first race as a race engineer, and he picked a fairly complicated race to do that.

"That was not his choice – but jokes aside, I think he really did an excellent job."

[Article continues below]

Effusive praise for Hart

Expanding on his initial assessment, Mekies shared how well Hart handled the flow of information and communication between Verstappen and the rest of his performance team.

"First qualifying, first race, he has managed to channel very well the work of the engineering teams behind him to Max," he explained.

"Of course the race was a complicated race, and we are probably a bit frustrated with the P3, which is the good news, but I really think he did an excellent job, and he was very well supported by GP as well in the background.

"You cannot recreate a relationship in no time, but I have every confidence that we are going to see him ramping up and building that relationship with Max.

"As part of our plan, we will alternate Tom and GP to the end of the year. It's a combination of other considerations; it's what we do with FP1 drivers and so forth and so on. It’s just part of the plan."

title: Lewis Hamilton pinpoints where he lost out on 'awesome' Max Verstappen fight
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton believes his lack of pace in the first two stints in the United States GP cost him a shot at Max Verstappen's podium.

In the final stint, Hamilton had fresher tyres than Verstappen and was carving chunks of time out of the Red Bull on his hard compound rubber as he tried to steal away a podium finish.

Ultimately, Hamilton fell 1.020s short of passing the Dutchman, but his challenge was stunted by a late virtual safety car for Valtteri Bottas's stricken Cadillac.

Although the VSC gave Verstappen a lifeline and reduced the green flag laps Hamilton had to attack, the Ferrari driver felt that the lack of pace and understeer in his SF-26 in the first two stints had left him with too much to recover in his final charge back to fourth place - including a pass on Lando Norris.

"I think probably I would have got to have a little bit of a battle with Max maybe in the last couple of laps," Hamilton told media, including RacingNews365, when directly asked if the VSC had cost him a podium.

"That would have been awesome, but it was all the result of the first two stints [that I was behind].

"I just lost so much ground, and I can't be giving up that time in the future; I really feel happy with how I drove.

"But it just took two whole stints to try and get this car to turn, and then once it started to turn in the third stint, I was back on the pace with the cars ahead.

"It was 18 seconds to [race-winner Antonelli] ahead, and those guys were obviously very quick, so I've just got to work on that."

[Article continues below]

Second place fight heats up

Following the Austin race, the fight for the runner-up spot in the drivers' championship has closed up.

Four drivers are now within just nine points of each other, with George Russell leading the way but Charles Leclerc within striking distance, with Hamilton and Verstappen sandwiched between.

title: Lando Norris returns to F2 after clinching coveted entry
excerpt:
Formula 2 has confirmed the 11 teams that will make up the grid for the 2027 season, which includes Lando Norris' squad.

Earlier this year, Norris announced the formation of the LN4 Fusion team after taking over selected assets of AIX Racing, setting itself up for entries in various junior categories.

It was already confirmed that the team would partake in the Formula 3 championship, but its junior championship participation has now extended to F2, seen as the last stepping stone before F1.

As expected, LN4 Fusion takes over the entry previously held by AIX Racing, with no other new entries confirmed for the 2027-2029 cycle.

"We received strong interest from teams around the world for this new three-year cycle, underlining the strength and appeal of our Championship," said F2 CEO Bruno Michel.

"We have retained ten of our current teams, who have consistently demonstrated their commitment to providing the best possible environment for young drivers to prepare for Formula 1.

"I am also pleased to welcome LN4 Fusion to the grid.

"They will bring considerable expertise, and I am confident they will make a valuable contribution to the Championship."

LN4 Fusion will race under an Italian licence, but has not yet announced the two drivers that will form its line-up.

In F3, the squad has confirmed that James Egozi, Gabriel Gomez and Dion Gowda will occupy the seats.

title: Charles Leclerc voices Ferrari concern after identifying key victory-costing moment
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc has declared that Ferrari is "not robust enough" over a full race weekend, identifying qualifying as the moment his hopes of winning the United States Grand Prix disappeared.

Leclerc started fourth at the Circuit of the Americas after a difficult Saturday but recovered to finish second, 13 seconds behind race winner Kimi Antonelli.

The Monegasque driver had topped the timesheets across the first two free practice sessions, and in Q2, only to see that pace evaporate when it mattered most in Q3, where he qualified fourth, two-and-a-half tenths of a second off Antonelli's pole time.

Victory returned to the conversation during the race itself, with Ferrari committing Leclerc to an aggressive two-stop strategy that exploited strong late pace on the hard compound.

It was enough for Leclerc to pass Max Verstappen in the closing stages and claim second, even as Antonelli's one-stop approach from pole kept him out of reach at the front.

Speaking in parc fermé, the Ferrari driver called it a satisfying result but one that fell short of the ultimate goal.

"It was quite a good race," he reflected after getting out of his car. "Unfortunately, we came short of the victory, which is eventually our target.

"But at the end of the day, it was a positive race. We had good pace. The first stint was a little bit more difficult. Kimi went for a one-stop, which was not really on our cards, to be honest.

"But we were in the race with Max, and we had good pace. It was a fun race, with quite nice battles at the start and then later on with Lando [Norris] and Max."

Later, in the post-race top three press conference, Leclerc pinpointed where the weekend went wrong, telling media, including RacingNews365, that Ferrari's qualifying struggles were the decisive factor.

"If you look at FP1, FP2 and FP3, we were very strong," Leclerc said. "If you look at qualifying, at the end of the day in Q3, it was extremely difficult to bring the tyres up to temperature, and we probably lost a shot at the victory there.

"Kimi was very strong, so, yeah, as a whole weekend, I think we're just not robust enough."

title: Bridgestone CEO sets 'number one' mission as Formula E partnership commences
excerpt:
RacingNews365 spoke with Bridgestone CEO Yasuhiro Morita following the announcement of the Japanese marque's return to an FIA World Championship.

Bridgestone will return to an FIA world championship for the first time since quitting Formula 1 in 2010, with the Japanese manufacturer's CEO setting out a mission to reclaim the "number one" position in the tyre industry after the firm was confirmed as Formula E's sole tyre supplier for the championship's upcoming Gen4 era.

The Japanese manufacturer departed grand prix racing at the end of the 2010 season, shifting its global motorsport focus towards sponsoring the Olympics and Paralympics instead.

But that chapter has now closed, with Bridgestone agreeing a four-season deal running from the 2026/27 campaign through to 2029/30, replacing Hankook as Formula E's tyre supplier.

Bridgestone CEO Yasuhiro Morita has explained that the pull back towards top-level motorsport came from within the company itself.

"It's obviously very exciting," Morita told RacingNews365 in an interview. "After we left Formula 1 in 2010, we supported the Olympics, Paralympics and other sporting events. It was also wonderful for us as a very strong global platform.

"What was missing was a product at the centre of that support. So that does, in some sense, but not really directly, help us improve our technologies. So we wondered some years ago, when we were ending the Olympic sponsorship, what could be next?

"And most of our team-mates, I would say, I don't know, I didn't count, but about 99%, I would say, really said, 'We want to go back, we want to go back to an FIA World Championship.'

"Bridgestone is a global company, not a local company, and everybody wants to go back. So the voice of the employees is there, and that helps me and the management teams to move forward with this."

Bridgestone CEO draws similarities to 1997 F1 arrival

Morita joined Bridgestone in April 1996, meaning he was with the company throughout its entire F1 spell, from its arrival in 1997 to its exit in 2010.

Asked whether leading the firm's return to an FIA world championship felt like a personal and emotional moment, Morita drew a direct line between where Bridgestone stood when he joined and where it stands now.

"So we were trying to be number one at that time, and Formula 1 was a challenge," he said.

"Nobody wanted to use our tyres in the first few seasons, and after that, we became number one in Formula 1. But today, many things have progressed. So it's not because of Formula 1 or Formula 1 alone, but today, where we are is number two.

"So I feel the same as when I joined Bridgestone in 1996: try to be number one. We are not number one. We are number two. Let's be number one. What do we need to do? And then that goes along with [joining Formula E]. So for me, it's a really emotional moment. And with all the team-mates, we want to grow again."

Bridgestone currently sits second behind Michelin in global tyre manufacturer rankings, having previously held the top spot for 11 years before losing it in 2021.

The Formula E deal, however, may not be the full extent of Bridgestone's ambitions. According to RacingNews365 sources, the manufacturer is actively pushing for a return to F1 as well, targeting the tender for the 2029 season and holding exploratory discussions within the paddock at both the Singapore and United States Grands Prix the past couple weeks.

title: McLaren reveal Lando Norris 'superpower' behind team order swap
excerpt:
Andrea Stella has explained why McLaren ordered Oscar Piastri to let Lando Norris through early in the United States GP, revealing that the team identified a specific trait that made the swap worthwhile.

McLaren has credited Lando Norris' "superpower" for the team's decision to swap him ahead of Oscar Piastri during the United States Grand Prix.

Norris passed his team-mate on lap eight at the Circuit of the Americas after Piastri was effectively told to cede position, with the Briton going on to finish fifth while the Australian came home seventh.

Team principal Andrea Stella said Norris had looked quicker than Piastri throughout the weekend at a circuit whose bumps and shifting grip levels tend to suit a more reactive driving style.

Speaking to the media, including RacingNews365, Stella said: "We had seen during the weekend that Lando was a little bit faster than Oscar.

"It is a track on which Lando excels, and is one of the tracks on which Oscar struggles a little more. This year, in particular for Oscar, is tricky because Oscar's superpower is to build.

"Once he creates references, he can really, effectively build lap after lap. But every lap [at COTA] is different, and these are the conditions that challenge Oscar.

"And they are the conditions where Lando uses his own superpower, which is being very adaptive to the conditions, especially as the car slides.

"Given this context, we discussed before the race that if Lando was behind Oscar, and Oscar could not keep up with the cars ahead, then we could give Lando a chance to see if we could attack the cars ahead, and that's what we did."

[Article continues below]

McLaren 'reinforced' particular point

Stella framed the decision as evidence that both drivers remain committed to McLaren's collective interests following the tension of Singapore, where the team principal had previously called the sprint clash a serious compromise of the constructors' effort against Red Bull.

Norris' attempted move at Turn 5 spun Piastri into the wall and triggered an internal review at Woking.

McLaren chose not to sanction Norris for that incident after he accepted responsibility, but the team made clear the lessons from Singapore were still fresh when the swap decision was made in Austin.

"It's a way of demonstrating that, as a team and together with the drivers, we care about the interest of the team, which is always the conversation that we have had, and especially after Singapore," said Stella.

"We reinforced how much it is important that, all together, we help McLaren get back to the position that we want to have, which is Oscar and Lando on the first row in qualifying, fighting for the win, and then we manage the internal competition.

"But up to then, all together we need to sustain the trajectory of McLaren back to the front."

title: Audi make significant senior appointment as debut F1 season nears end
excerpt:
Audi Formula Racing has announced the appointment of Thomas Fuhr as its new CEO.

The German will take charge of the Neuburg-based company on November 1, and oversee Audi's entire F1 project.

The appointment comes as Audi winds down its debut season in the sport, one that sees it currently sit eighth in the constructors' championship.

Fuhr brings more than three decades of international engineering and leadership experience to the role.

The team has detailed that Fuhr's appointment allows Stefan Dreyer, Audi Formula Racing's Chief Technology Officer, to focus solely on leading the technical development of the Audi F1 power unit.

Christian Foyer, the company's Chief Operating Officer, will continue to oversee day-to-day operations at the Neuburg site.

Fuhr's background includes a stint as Managing Director of Mercedes-AMG High Performance Powertrains between 2009 and 2012.

“We have built strong foundations in Neuburg, developing Audi’s first Formula 1 power unit from the ground up,” said Audi team principal Mattia Binotto.

“As Thomas understands both the technical challenge and what it takes to build and lead high-performing teams, I am confident he will play a key role by further developing the team and its organisation to make us the best F1 manufacturer.

“I am very much looking forward to welcoming him to the team.”

title: Toto Wolff launches strong George Russell defence after 'wonderkid' realisation
excerpt:
Toto Wolff has issued a strong defence of George Russell's capabilities after criticism from Helmut Marko about his performances.

Although Russell dominated the season-opener in Australia, the Mercedes driver has endured a torrid year and has been unable to consistently access performance from the W17, with three grand prix wins to team-mate Kimi Antonelli on nine.

Antonelli is now almost certain to win the world championship in just his second season of F1, and holds a 123-point advantage over Russell with just 125 remaining heading to Mexico City - where if Russell fails to win, Antonelli will be champion by default.

If he does win, Antonelli just requires a ninth-place finish or better to be crowned F1's youngest champion.

As Russell has struggled to consistently find performance and constantly had to tweak his driving style, former Red Bull advisor Helmut Marko claimed he doubts "whether Russell will ever have another chance at the world title or be given number one status anywhere."

When these comments were put to Wolff, he staunchly defended his driver - and pointed out the other factor of the mental challenge Russell faced at dealing with the unstoppable momentum of Antonelli earlier in the season.

Russell entered the campaign as the bookies' favourite for the title, a position only strengthened by his commanding performance in Melbourne to kick off the year, before "wonderkid" Antonelli then rattled off five straight wins between China and Monaco to open up a 68-point lead after the Principality that Russell has never recovered from.

"I respect Helmut's opinion, but he is wrong about George," Wolff told media, including RacingNews365.

"George has all the ability, but the car doesn't suit him.

"I think at the beginning of the season, it is maybe difficult to cope with a situation when you're feeling like 'this is my year' and then we have this wonderkid on the other side that really starts to chip away [at you].

"I believe that in a new season, George, if we provide him with a quick car, he absolutely has what it takes to win an F1 championship.

"I think it is a bit too easy to forget about all the years he won in F2, F3 and his rookie years and the back-to-back titles in the European karting championships.

"That is all still there."

[Article continues below]

Mercedes pledge fix

Wolff is also keen on Mercedes "working" with Russell to diagnose exactly what it is he is struggling with in the W17.

The Austrian was firm that it is "absolutely not the case" that Russell should be half-a-second slower than Antonelli - as he pledged to work with the Briton.

title: Red Bull responds to F1 rival talk speculation over supplying engines
excerpt:
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has denied that "serious conversations" are taking place with any rival F1 teams over supplying power units, but did not rule out the possibility in the future.

Mekies did not go as far as refuting that any talks are happening with Aston Martin, with the Silverstone-based squad at the centre of recent speculation that it could ditch Honda for Red Bull Powertrains (RBPT) as early as 2028.

Aston Martin chief trackside officer Mike Krack believes the team will still be with the Japanese marque when it wins its first grand prix in F1, but with the partnership sputtering straight out of the gates, the rumours came as no real surprise.

Red Bull, on the other hand, has enjoyed a much more fruitful start to life in collaboration with Ford, and the team's fledgling internal combustion engine has defied expectations, including being established as the benchmark in the FIA's additional development and upgrade opportunities (ADUO) programme.

Although the Milton Keynes-based team has questioned the motorsport governing body on how that conclusion was reached, given the dominance of the Mercedes power unit overall, it underlines how impressive the early returns of the project have been, something that has in part triggered the recent flurry of reports.

When speculation that RBPT could supply Aston Martin from 2028 was put to Mekies, and he was asked whether he was in a position to deny any talks between the parties, the Frenchman shut down any immediate possibility, but did not rule it out altogether.

"Look, we got a lot of unwanted positive publicity about the performance of our engine, and that certainly came with attention from a lot of teams," the Red Bull team principal told media, including RacingNews365.

"Are we having any serious conversations with anyone to supply another team? No. We don't feel we are ready for that.

"Is it set in stone for the next five years? No, because I don't know what's going to happen in the next five years."

[Article continues below]

When might Red Bull consider becoming a power unit provider?

With enhancing the power unit restricted to software updates and better integration and understanding, unless granted development tokens through ADUO, Red Bull has nonetheless made significant strides over the season.

Mekies insisted that the primary focus remains on improving the power unit and not selling it to potential customers, with considerable work still to be done, even if RBPT cannot develop the hardware — as the benchmark team — at this stage.

He said: "But for sure, for us, there is enough work to do on our side to improve the power unit, to improve its integration in the car, and to get to the level of the best competitors before considering being able to supply one more team on top of Racing Bulls.

Tellingly, he added that "nothing will change in the next year or so", which fits conveniently with the rumoured 2028 timeframe for Aston Martin to purchase a supply.

title: Lewis Hamilton declares 'pivotal moment' as Ferrari instructions issued
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has declared Ferrari to be in a "pivotal moment" with the design of its 2027 F1 challenger.

Work is already underway across the grid on designing and manufacturing the machines for next season, with just five grands prix remaining in the season.

Whilst Hamilton's Ferrari looks set to finish as runners-up to Mercedes, in the drivers' fight, he is engaged with George Russell, Max Verstappen, and team-mate Charles Leclerc in a tough fight for second place, with just nine points separating the four drivers.

In a final bid to get ahead, Ferrari unveiled its final upgrade of the season in the United States, which proved to be a strong weekend for the team, although a poor qualifying ruined its chances of fighting Kimi Antonelli for the win as Leclerc translated fourth on the grid into second place and Hamilton turned fifth into fourth - although it would have been third if not for a late VSC denying him a chance at attacking Verstappen.

Ferrari's SF-26 has been regarded as the best chassis on the grid in 2026, with GPS data proving that through the corners, it is the best machine and ahead of the Mercedes W17, Red Bull RB22 or McLaren MCL40.

With attention quickly turning to the new season, Hamilton declared Ferrari as being in a "pivotal moment."

"I feel like the team have been doing a really, really good job, and in the background, I'm working on this pivotal moment in terms of steering the car in the right direction for next year," Hamilton told media, including RacingNews365.

"I'm really working on the areas that we need to improve for next year's car and that's partly the discussion over the next couple of weekends and giving feedback to the guys who are designing the parts for next year.

"[I am] pointing out to them where we can improve on the actual chassis side and the aerodynamic package, and of course, they're working hard to improve our engine for next year.

"I think if we're able to get to the [Mercedes and Red Bull power units] with the engine, we're obviously going to be fighting for wins in the races."

[Article continues below]

Hamilton explains Ferrari focus

Further explaining the work going on at Maranello for the 2027 machine, Hamilton spoke of the "subtle" changes he felt were required.

"It started probably a month ago, but this is the time where you actually start needing to make decisions and saying: 'Okay, these are the areas we're losing [out in]," he said.

"'These are the areas that if you fix for next year, [it is worth] half a tenth in every corner', and these are the areas that we're struggling with.

"'[Or] this is where I want the aero balance to be for next year,' but there is not a huge amount of things.

"I think we've got a really good package, so it is keeping the good things on the car, and rectifying a couple of these small, subtle differences."
